implementation.canonicalReads: Server-only tenant-scoped DAL for envelopes, goals, transactions, accounts, bills, debts, allocation plan/rules and stored period. Per-entity readers are request-cached and the aggregate uses an explicit RepeatableRead transaction. Invalid tenant identifiers fail before querying; legacy NULL-owner periods remain excluded. Reads never write, seed, or fall back to memory. Failures remain distinguishable through adapters/actions/advisor/opportunities/search. Caller-visible errors are stable codes or fixed messages, and server diagnostics omit raw query and connection values. Row DTOs/aggregate are shallow-frozen; arrays and Dates are mutable. Independent re-review pending; persistence is not deposit confirmation or full financial correctness.
implementation.deferredReaders: Still process-local after FIN-01: the /transactions and /calendar display pages, vault/mock-data.ts, and the memory seeders in store.ts. Three mutually inconsistent expense/auto predicates also remain (mock.ts isAuto, store.ts isAuto, forecast/spending-trends.ts SQL rule); unifying them is a convention change, not a read refactor. Transaction.cleared remains an unwritten dead column; wiring it is FIN-05. Advisor simulate/paycheck paths still use legacy memory state.
implementation.settlementSemantics: Income confirmation is unknown. apply-paycheck writes source "recurring" for a cron-created paycheck and "manual" for a user-clicked one; log-transaction writes "manual" for a user-logged entry. All are creation provenance. No stored field records settlement, so nothing may infer received/settled/available cash.
implementation.readFailureSemantics: A failed financial read is distinguishable at every layer. The DAL returns a stable code (read-failed / invalid-tenant-id) and never err.message; liveEnvelopesFromDb and liveGoalsFromDb rethrow sanitized errors as they did before FIN-01; listEnvelopesForAction returns a typed error result; advisor tools return ok:false with fixed strings; topOpportunities throws; the command-palette branch rejects. Proven by induced-failure tests in tests/smoke-financial-state.mjs (78 checks).

Canonical financial-state reads move to a server-only Data Access Layer (src/lib/state/financial-state.ts) querying Prisma, following the installed Next data-security guide. Three consequences are normative, not incidental. (1) The aggregate reads inside ONE explicit RepeatableRead transaction: Postgres defaults to READ COMMITTED, under which each statement may observe a different commit, so wrapping reads in prisma.$transaction alone would NOT give a coherent snapshot. This is a read-consistency decision only; no writer, allocation rule or ledger behaviour changes. (2) Settlement is UNKNOWN: Transaction.source is creation provenance and Transaction.cleared is stored but never written, so neither evidences a deposit. Income carries confirmation:"unknown" and no reader may infer received/settled/available from source, isPrimaMateria or cleared. FIN-05 owns writer semantics plus migration and backfill. (3) The three inconsistent definitions of expense/auto-written (mock.ts, store.ts, forecast/spending-trends.ts) are deliberately NOT unified here; that is a financial-convention change with its own revision.

FIN-01 revision 2, after Polar's changes_requested review. A read failure must remain DISTINGUISHABLE at every changed caller, not only inside the DAL. The first revision tagged the DAL result and then had three callers convert it to an empty list, so a database outage looked like an empty account and the advisor's handler contract ('empty means you have no envelopes') would have told the user their money was gone. Now: the mock.ts adapters rethrow a sanitized error exactly as they did before FIN-01; listEnvelopesForAction returns a typed error result; the advisor returns ok:false with a fixed message; topOpportunities throws; the command-palette branch rejects through its existing Promise.all. Separately, raw database errors must never leave the server: the DAL returns one of two stable codes (read-failed / invalid-tenant-id) and logs the underlying error server-side only, because Prisma connection text carries host, port, user name and invocation text and the advisor serialises its error into the LLM's tool result, which reaches the user. Throwing rather than widening topOpportunities' return type is what keeps this inside its file scope, since src/app/page.tsx and learn/your-numbers call it. For N2 the action's contract is widened to PlanetId | null instead of substituting a planet: no caller of listEnvelopesForAction exists in src, and NewTransactionForm already types planet as nullable, so no scope extension was required.
